samples.summary: `PUT .../freeze` still accepts up to 1,000,000 frozen rows, which this change's own reasoning calls an unpaintable tab — a stored client-side DoS the new snap cap explicitly delegates to this validator and this validator does not enforce
samples.evidence: Chain: (1) `parseFreeze` bounds `rows` only at the grid (`max: MaxRows` = 1_000_000, worksheet-settings.ts:61) and `cols` at 18_278. (2) `ApiV1WorksheetController.setFreeze` (worksheet.controller.ts:121-128) passes the requested value through `snapFreezePastMerges`, which by design leaves a caller-requested line untouched — merging.ts:355-362 only bounds *growth*, and its own docstring says "bounding the request is the validator's job (`parseFreeze` in the backend)". (3) The value is persisted verbatim and loaded with no clamp: `Sheet.loadFreezePane` (sheet.ts:567-571) and `YorkieStore.getFreezePane` (yorkie-store.ts:1221-1227). (4) `GridCanvas.render` draws quadrant B/A with `renderQuadrantCells(ctx, 1, fr + 1, ...)` (gridcanvas.ts:329-332, 400-405) and that helper loops `for (let row = rowStart; row <= rowEnd; row++)` over every column (gridcanvas.ts:869, 1754) with no viewport clipping of the loop. Attack: any principal with write scope on the workspace (including a leaked/over-scoped API key) issues one `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:w/documents/:d/tabs/:t/freeze {"rows":1000000}`; every collaborator who opens that tab afterwards builds ~1e6 x visible-columns srefs per frame and the grid never paints — and per `MaxSnappedFreeze`'s own docstring (merging.ts:45-59) the user "cannot reach the freeze menu to undo it". Recovery requires another API call. The 1,000-row ceiling this PR introduces for the *snap* concedes that 100,000 is already fatal, so the direct request path is 1,000x more permissive than the derived path in the same change.

samples.summary: `snapFreezePastMerges` calls `parseRef` on merge keys read straight from the CRDT with no try/catch or round-trip check, so a single malformed key wedges `PUT freeze` with a 500 — the exact threat model this change hardened `rebuildMergeCoverMap` against
samples.evidence: merging.ts:346-348 does `parseRef(anchorSref)` on every stored key; `parseRef` throws a bare `Error('Invalid Reference')` (coordinates.ts:350-352, 363-365) for a key with no digit. This helper is now reached server-side from `ApiV1WorksheetController.setFreeze` (worksheet.controller.ts:121) and from `shiftWorksheetViewState` (worksheet-structure.ts:278). The same PR states the attacker model explicitly — `Sheet.rebuildMergeCoverMap` (sheet.ts, `rebuildMergeCoverMap`) now wraps `parseRef` in try/catch and adds a `toSref(anchor) !== anchorSref` round-trip because "the Yorkie auth webhook authorizes a write by (document, verb) and never inspects an op's content, so anyone holding `rw` on the document can put an arbitrary merge map into it directly". The server-side copy got neither guard. Attack: a collaborator with `rw` (or a compromised editor session) writes `merges: {"x": {rs:2,cs:2}}` directly through the CRDT; from then on `PUT .../freeze` on that tab throws a non-HttpException inside `doc.update` and returns 500 for every caller including the owner, permanently. `PUT merges` cannot repair it without first succeeding, and `POST insert`/`delete` share the same throw via `shiftMergeMap`/`snapFreezePastMerges`. Note the browser is protected by the new defensive load and the API body path by `parseMerges`; only the server-side read of already-stored data is unguarded.

samples.summary: The merge budget is enforced only on writers; the backend reads and now additionally sorts the stored merge map unbounded inside a synchronous `doc.update`, so an oversized map written directly to the CRDT stalls the shared Node event loop on every insert/delete/freeze
samples.evidence: `mergeBudgetAdmits`/`mergeBudgetError` are spent by writers only (parseMerges, YorkieStore.setMerge, the importer, canMergeSelection). Nothing on the backend validates the map it reads back: `shiftWorksheetViewState` (worksheet-structure.ts:278-282) and `ApiV1WorksheetController.setFreeze` (worksheet.controller.ts:121) hand the whole stored map to `snapFreezePastMerges`, which materializes one `Range` per entry and then copies-and-sorts the array once per axis (merging.ts:345-348, 357). Both run synchronously inside `doc.update` in the shared backend process. By the change's own threat model an `rw` holder can write a merge map of arbitrary size straight into the CRDT (no content inspection in the Yorkie auth webhook), so a map of, say, 1e6 entries turns each `POST insert` / `POST delete` / `PUT freeze` into an O(n log n) walk plus two full array copies that blocks the event loop for *all* tenants — unlike the browser-side walk, which only costs the attacking client. The client-side defensive clamp added to `rebuildMergeCoverMap` has no server-side counterpart.
searchedFor: grep mergeBudgetAdmits / mergeBudgetError / mergeBudgetOf across all packages
checked packages/backend/src/main.ts for body limits and global throttler config

samples.summary: The backend legacy-shape migration copies an unvalidated merges map and sizes the axis arrays from merge extents, bypassing the budget this change claims every writer spends — and amplifying a 1-entry map into a million CRDT axis entries
samples.evidence: `cloneMergeRecord` (worksheet-shape-migration.ts:86-96) copies a legacy `merges` record verbatim into the migrated worksheet with no `mergeBudgetAdmits` call, and `maxIndexFromMerges` (worksheet-shape-migration.ts:250-267) derives `maxRow`/`maxCol` from `ref.r + span.rs - 1`, feeding `buildAxisOrder(prefix, length)` which does `Array.from({length}, ...)` (line 303-305). A legacy-shaped root holding `merges: {"A1": {rs: 1000000, cs: 1}}` — writable by any `rw` holder through the CRDT, the same door the PR documents for the merge map — makes the migration materialize a 1,000,000-element `rowOrder` array into the document, and `maxIndexFromMerges` also calls bare `parseRef` on each key (line 260), throwing on a malformed one. This is a pre-existing path, but it is a writer of `merges` outside the newly claimed universal budget, so the docs' 'every writer spends the budget' invariant is not actually closed.

verdict.reason: Every link in the reviewer's chain checks out against the repository. parseFreeze (worksheet-settings.ts:58-64) bounds rows only at MaxRows=1000000 (line 16), despite its own docstring (lines 50-57) saying the reason for the bound is that frozen quadrants render with no viewport clipping. setFreeze (worksheet.controller.ts:98-134) hands the requested value to snapFreezePastMerges, whose sweep returns an unmodified caller-requested line (merging.ts:355-362) — the MaxSnappedFreeze release at line 361 is gated on `snapped !== line`, so it bounds growth only, and the docstring at merging.ts:56-58 explicitly delegates bounding of the request to parseFreeze. The value is then stored and read back with no clamp (sheet.ts:567-571; yorkie-store.ts:1221-1227; layout.ts:136-153; worksheet.ts:454-462). GridCanvas.render draws quadrants B and A with rowStart=1, rowEnd=fr+1 (gridcanvas.ts:329-334, 400-405), and buildRenderableRefs loops every row in that band across every column, allocating a Ref and a toSref per cell (gridcanvas.ts:869-878); the ctx.clip() at line 328 clips painting, not the loop. No guard exists on any path between the validator and the render loop, so one authorized PUT with rows=1000000 persists a tab that no collaborator can paint or un-freeze through the UI. No named refutation ground applies: the code is present exactly as described, nothing guards it, and a stored cross-collaborator DoS via unbounded API input is within the security lens.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding is verifiable in the tree. merging.ts:346-348 calls parseRef(anchorSref) on each stored merge key with no try/catch and no toSref round-trip; parseRef throws a bare Error('Invalid Reference') for a key with no digit (coordinates.ts:350-352) or a NaN parse (coordinates.ts:363-365). That helper is reached server-side on data read straight from the CRDT: worksheet.controller.ts:121-125 feeds it safeWorksheetRecordEntries(ws.merges ?? {}) inside doc.update, and worksheet-record.ts:47-61 shows that helper only recovers from duplicate-ownKeys TypeErrors and does zero key validation. The same unguarded call is reached from shiftWorksheetViewState (worksheet-structure.ts:278-282), invoked by applyWorksheetShift (worksheet-structure.ts:611) which the insert/delete endpoint calls (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:355). The claimed asymmetry is real: Sheet.rebuildMergeCoverMap (sheet.ts:888-900) wraps parseRef in try/catch AND rejects non-round-tripping keys, with a comment at sheet.ts:866-872 spelling out the exact threat model ('anyone holding rw on the document can put an arbitrary merge map into it directly'). parseMerges (worksheet-settings.ts:136-149) validates keys only for the request body, never for stored data. The attacker model is confirmed by yorkie-auth.controller.ts:329-334, which authorizes purely by document key plus method/verb and never inspects op content. A malformed key written through the CRDT therefore makes a non-HttpException escape doc.update, 500-ing PUT freeze and POST insert/delete permanently for all callers including the owner. No guard elsewhere makes this unreachable; this is unsafe handling of attacker-controlled stored input causing a persistent denial of service, squarely in the security lens.

finding.summary: The new merge-map budget is enforced only on write paths; the load-time walk it exists to protect (`rebuildMergeCoverMap`) is still uncapped, so any principal with document write access can brick a tab via the CRDT
finding.evidence: All four new enforcement points are write-side and two of them are client code: `parseMerges` (backend `PUT merges`), `YorkieStore.setMerge` (browser), `Sheet.canMergeSelection`/`applyPasteMerges` (browser), and the XLSX importer (browser). Nothing validates merge-map *content* on the server for the collaborative path: `packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts` only answers the Yorkie auth webhook with (key, verb) allow/deny — it never inspects document ops. So a user who legitimately holds `rw` on a shared document (an invited editor, or a share-link editor) can attach with the Yorkie SDK, or a patched/older build of the frontend, and write `sheets[tab].merges = { A1: { rs: 1000000, cs: 18278 }, ... }` directly. `Sheet.loadMerges()` (sheet.ts:588) then calls `rebuildMergeCoverMap()` (sheet.ts:862), which loops `for r in rs { for c in cs { mergeCoverMap.set(...) } }` with no cap and no bail-out, on every collaborator's next open — including the workspace owner's. Result is a permanently unopenable tab: exactly the outcome `MaxMergedCells`'s own docstring calls "a document nobody can open again", and exactly what `docs/design/sheets/sheet.md` now asserts "cannot be created in the first place". The write-side caps raise the bar for the REST client while leaving the CRDT door open, and the new `mergeBudget` field is computed *after* the unbounded walk has already run, so it cannot stop it. Mitigation would be a cap at load (clamp/skip in `rebuildMergeCoverMap`/`loadMerges`) or server-side op validation, not only at the writers.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the load-time walk `rebuildMergeCoverMap` is uncapped and that every enforcement point is write-side. Reading the function shows the opposite: sheet.ts:882 opens a local budget, sheet.ts:887 calls `mergeBudgetAdmits(budget, [span])` and `continue`s BEFORE the nested cover loops at sheet.ts:905-911, and sheet.ts:902-903 accumulates the budget across anchors so the cumulative caps apply as well. `mergeBudgetAdmits` (merging.ts:104-118) rejects any span with rs*cs > MaxMergedCells (100000, merging.ts:14) and, via `mergeBudgetError` (merging.ts:86-94), any map exceeding MaxMergeEntries (10000) or MaxMergeCoveredCells (1000000). The exact CRDT payload the finding names, `{rs: 1000000, cs: 18278}`, is therefore discarded after one multiply-and-compare and never reaches `mergeCoverMap.set`; over-budget spans are additionally dropped from the in-memory map at sheet.ts:913-915. `loadMerges()` (sheet.ts:588-591) routes the unvalidated collaborative map from `YorkieStore.getMerges` (yorkie-store.ts:1068-1076) directly into that guarded rebuild, and the same guard covers the shift/move rebuilds at sheet.ts:1425 and sheet.ts:1650. The doc comment at sheet.ts:859-878 states this read-side defense verbatim, citing the same threat model (Yorkie auth webhook authorizes by document+verb and never inspects op content) the reviewer used. The sub-claim that `mergeBudget` is computed after an unbounded walk is also inverted: sheet.ts:916 merely records the budget the guarded walk already spent. One unraised residual (a degenerate cs:0 span with huge rs passes line 887 with cells=0 while the outer r loop still spins) is a different payload and a separate finding, not the absence claim under review.
